context: A uni student interviews a retired diplomat at home
purpose: Teach: 祖国/敵対/全日本/肖像/風水/ハンガリー/鳥取/徳島

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間をいただきありがとうございます。早速ですが、長年祖国を離れての勤務、どんなお気持ちでしたか。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. To start, how did it feel to work so long away from your homeland?
lines.style: Polite, respectful interview opener with slight nervousness in tone, formal university-student register.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そうだなあ、若い頃はハンガリーに駐在していてね。ブダペストの街並みは今も忘れられんよ。
lines.en: Well, in my younger days I was stationed in Hungary. I still can't forget the streets of Budapest.
lines.style: Warm, nostalgic elderly voice, slow pace with reflective sighs between phrases.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 壁にかかっている肖像画は、もしかして当時の大使の方ですか。
lines.en: Is the portrait hanging on the wall perhaps the ambassador from that time?
lines.style: Curious, slightly impressed, leaning forward with genuine student interest.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、あれは恩師でね。冷戦の頃は敵対する国々の間で、言葉一つに神経を使ったものだ。
lines.en: Ah, that's my mentor. During the Cold War, between hostile nations, we agonized over every single word.
lines.style: Gravely serious shift in tone, voice deepening as he recalls tense diplomatic memories.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 退官された今は、鳥取のご実家と東京を行き来されていると伺いました。
lines.en: I heard that now in retirement you move between your family home in Tottori and Tokyo.
lines.style: Conversational pivot to lighter topic, friendly and inquisitive student tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そう、妻が徳島の出だから、四国にもよく顔を出す。この家は風水を見てもらって建てたんだよ。
lines.en: Yes, my wife is from Tokushima, so we visit Shikoku often. This house was built after consulting feng shui.
lines.style: Relaxed, slightly chuckling, proud homeowner sharing personal anecdotes warmly.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: へえ、意外です。学生時代は全日本剣道大会にも出られたとか、本当ですか。
lines.en: Wow, that's surprising. I also heard you competed in the All-Japan Kendo Championship as a student. Is that true?
lines.style: Genuinely surprised exclamation, voice rising with admiration and youthful enthusiasm.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若気の至りさ。外交も剣道も、結局は忍耐と相手への敬意に尽きるね。
lines.en: Just the folly of youth. In the end, both diplomacy and kendo come down to patience and respect for your opponent.
lines.style: Quiet wisdom in voice, philosophical and measured, ending the interview with gentle gravitas.
